findings.text: the leading-assignment scan reads only assignments that begin a segment, so `env GIT_DIR=<other>/.git GIT_WORK_TREE=<other> git reset --hard` is allowed (hook exit 0) and moved the other checkout's HEAD in bypass-probe.log.
`cd -` is resolved as the current directory, so `cd <other> && cd <worktree> && cd - && git reset --hard` is allowed (hook exit 0) and moved the other checkout's HEAD in bypass-probe.log.
only `cd` is tracked as a directory change, so `pushd <other> >/dev/null && git reset --hard` is allowed (hook exit 0) and moved the other checkout's HEAD in bypass-probe.log.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against base 2cd573f1; 8d515f5e adds the guard, the install opt-in and 7 tests, c9ac064e appends the landing record, 9db0672b adds alias, assignment and nested-script resolution, the unparsable refusal and the sync wiring plus 6 tests, and 5a8f6ce6 appends the gap-closure record — the only deletions in the whole diff are 6 replaced lines in reckon/cli.py and reckon/hooks/install.py, and no plan-version or plan-modified meta line is touched.
item_verdicts.done_when: read; the done_when names the four behaviours, the installer emitting the entry without writing the settings file, and no added failures in the companion suites; the manifest records each with committed logs under docs/figures/a-worker-cannot-write-your-home/, and this review re-ran the named gate at the reviewed head from the reviewed worktree — 13 passed (recheck-head-tests.log, module resolved inside the reviewed worktree).
item_verdicts.goal: read the pointer's goal — a PreToolUse Bash guard, in scope only under RECKON_RUN_ID, refusing a mutating git verb against any repository but the run's worktree, with an installer entry and no install; the head guard refuses the four routes the previous review named (probe_bypass_routes.py: alias via -c alias.<name>=..., leading GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE, command substitution / backtick / bash -c / brace groups, unparsable forms) and emits its installer entry only under the opt-in, but three same-family routes are still allowed and each reaches another checkout, as the findings record.
item_verdicts.manifest: read at the run directory; it records the four commits, the gate with its base and head arms, the companion counts (39 either side), the lint delta (233 to 233), the negative-control log whose first line repeats the declaration verbatim, and the widen refusal in follow_ons; every claim I re-derived matched — the red arm's guard blob 4ecc0f0d equals git rev-parse c9ac064e:reckon/hooks/worker_git_guard.py, and render/my base cli.py carries the same two SIM findings as head.
item_verdicts.write_paths: read the dispatch's six granted paths from the reviewed run's live pointer and the manifest's orientation list; git diff --numstat 2cd573f1..5a8f6ce6 lists 21 files, every one inside the manifest's paths with 0 deletions on the two cumulative documents, and reckon/cli.py:187 lies outside the pointer's six granted paths — the single finding crew check-manifest reports and the manifest discloses in follow_ons.

justifications.evidence: the red arm's guard blob matches c9ac064e, the head arm and companion suites are committed under docs/figures/a-worker-cannot-write-your-home/, lint is 233 to 233 with the two cli.py findings present at base, and my recheck of tests/test_worker_git_guard.py at the reviewed head is 13 passed.

justifications.goal_fidelity: the four named routes are refused at reckon/hooks/worker_git_guard.py:501 while the routes in the findings — an env-prefixed assignment (worker_git_guard.py:237), cd - (worker_git_guard.py:263) and pushd (worker_git_guard.py:253) — reach hook exit 0 and move another checkout's HEAD.
